after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
A rectangular plate occupies the region
$D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,1\le y\le 2}$
with mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=3(x+y).$ Find the moment of inertia of this plate about the line $x=1.$
after.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=1$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-1|.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}3(x+y)|x-1{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}3(x+y)(x-1)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{3(x+y)^{2}}{2}(x-1)^{2}]}_{1}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3((x+2)^{2}-(x+1)^{2})}{2}(x-1)^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(2x+3)(x-1)^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(2{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}-4x+3)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{[\frac{{x}^{4}}{2}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}-2{x}^{2}+3x]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}((\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{3}-2+3)-0) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}(\frac{7}{6}) \\  & =\frac{7}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

A plate with mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region $D$ enclosed between the curves $y=1-{x}^{2}$ and $y=(x-1)^{2}$, as shown above. Given that the region has an area of $\frac{1}{3},$ find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $x=1.$
after.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,(x-1)^{2}\le y\le 1-{x}^{2}},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14095617/assets/de82c9b30dfb156dea8ace88e27f00887dcecf197e7a50493f34f6a08dfae161.png)

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=1$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-1|.
$$

Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=3M.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & =3M{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{(x-1)^{2}}^{1-{x}^{2}}|x-1{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =3M{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{(x-1)^{2}}^{1-{x}^{2}}(x-1)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =3M{\int }_{0}^{1}(x-1)^{2}[y]_{y=(x-1)^{2}}^{y=1-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3M{\int }_{0}^{1}(x-1)^{2}(1-{x}^{2}-(x-1)^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =3M{\int }_{0}^{1}-2{x}^{4}+6{x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}+2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =3M{[\frac{-2{x}^{5}}{5}+\frac{3{x}^{4}}{2}-2{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =3M(-\frac{2}{5}+\frac{3}{2}-2+1-0) \\  & =\frac{3M}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

A plate with mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region $D$ enclosed between the curves ${y}^{2}=2x$ and $y=x$, as shown above. Given that the region has an area of $\frac{2}{3},$ find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $y=2.$
after.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type II region with representation

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\,\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}\le x\le y},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14095617/assets/a34ed2c8c25aa5c3c1e28e4458e11779f6b5948acbebdcb6e05b5bf1257689d4.png)

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $y=2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|y-2|.
$$

Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=\frac{3M}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $y=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{{y}^{2}/2}^{y}\frac{3M}{2}|y-2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{{y}^{2}/2}^{y}(y-2)^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}(y-2)^{2}[x]_{x={y}^{2}/2}^{x=y}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}(y-2)^{2}(y-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3M}{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}(-{y}^{4}+6{y}^{3}-12{y}^{2}+8y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3M}{4}{[-\frac{{y}^{5}}{5}+\frac{3{y}^{4}}{2}-4{y}^{3}+4{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3M}{4}(-\frac{32}{5}+24-32+16-0) \\  & =\frac{6M}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, the distance between a point and the line $x=1$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-1|.
$$

Next, the mass density can be written as $\lambda (x,y)=ky,$ where $k$ is a constant of proportionality. We can find the value of $k$ by integrating the mass density function over the plate.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}ky\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =k({\int }_{-1}^{1}\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{1}^{2}y\,\text{d}y) \\  & =k\cdot {[x]}_{-1}^{1}\cdot {[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =k(1-(-1))(2-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =3k.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\lambda (x,y)=ky=\frac{M}{3}y.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{M}{3}y|x-1{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{M}{3}y(x-1)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{M}{3}({\int }_{-1}^{1}(x-1)^{2}\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{1}^{2}y\,\text{d}y) \\  & =\frac{M}{3}\cdot {[\frac{1}{3}(x-1)^{3}]}_{-1}^{1}\cdot {[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{M}{3}\cdot \frac{1}{3}(0-(-8))\cdot [\frac{1}{2}(4-1)] \\  & =\frac{M}{3}\cdot \frac{8}{3}\cdot \frac{3}{2} \\  & =\frac{4M}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 1,\,\,1-{x}^{2}\le y\le 2-2{x}^{2}},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14095617/assets/026b560b2e81899cb767930a5c63173e4a3489c6bc10b7148007127e132406c9.png)

Also, the distance between a point and the line $x=-1$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x+1|.
$$

Next, the mass density can be written as $\lambda (x,y)=k{x}^{2},$ where $k$ is a constant of proportionality. We can find the value of $k$ by integrating the mass density function over the plate.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{1-{x}^{2}}^{2-2{x}^{2}}k{x}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{-1}^{1}{[{x}^{2}y]}_{1-{x}^{2}}^{2-2{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{-1}^{1}{x}^{2}(2-2{x}^{2}-1+{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{-1}^{1}{x}^{2}(1-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =k\cdot {[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{5}{x}^{5}]}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =\frac{4k}{15}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\lambda (x,y)=k{x}^{2}=\frac{15}{4}M{x}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=-1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{1-{x}^{2}}^{2-2{x}^{2}}\frac{15}{4}M{x}^{2}|x+1{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{1-{x}^{2}}^{2-2{x}^{2}}\frac{15}{4}M{x}^{2}(x+1)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{15}{4}M{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{1-{x}^{2}}^{2-2{x}^{2}}({x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}+{x}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{15}{4}M{\int }_{-1}^{1}({x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}){\int }_{1-{x}^{2}}^{2-2{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{15}{4}M{\int }_{-1}^{1}({x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}+{x}^{2})[y]_{1-{x}^{2}}^{2-2{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{15}{4}M{\int }_{-1}^{1}({x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}+{x}^{2})(1-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{15}{4}M{\int }_{-1}^{1}(-{x}^{6}-2{x}^{5}+2{x}^{3}+{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{15}{4}M{[-\frac{1}{7}{x}^{7}-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{6}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}+\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =\frac{15}{4}M(-\frac{2}{7}+0+0+\frac{2}{3}) \\  & =\frac{15}{4}M\cdot \frac{8}{21} \\  & =\frac{10M}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$
